the protein kinase CK2 inhibitor TBB induces apoptosis in Jurkat cells, that the apoptotic response is preceded by inhibition in the phosphorylation of haemopoietic lineage-cell-specific protein 1, and that this protein is cleaved by caspases only when it is not phosphorylated.
the CK2 inhibitor TBB induces apoptosis and caspasemediated fragmentation of the CK2 protein substrate HS1 in Jurkat cells.
the inhibition of CK2 by TBB induces HS1 degradation and that this degradation is dependent on the activation of caspases.

the role of protein kinase CKII in the regulation of apoptosis and the possible involvement of HS1 in this process.

TBB, a specific inhibitor of CK2, is a promising tool to study the role of this enzyme in the regulation of cell death and survival.

CK2 inhibitors may represent novel anti-cancer drugs.
